$comment: Seconds each browser test file runs in one of CI's docs browser jobs (4 cores, the files several at a time, so the time a file takes beside others): what packages/tools/src/run-node-tests.js splits the files into TEST_SHARD's shares by (`--shard-weights`, apps/docs/package.json's test:browser), longest first, each to the share with the least so far. A file not named here weighs the median of these, and the log of its job says so. A name of a file that is not here is ignored. Measured again from CI runs 45896337474 and 45898416949 (2026-11-26, a pull request and a train: the `# file-duration` lines of the nine jobs of each that were green), the mean of the two. The files that ran only in the tenth job of those runs, which reached its time limit in both, have no such line there, and were measured locally on 2026-11-27: blueprint-pages, blueprint, example, heading-link, held-room-figures, held-room-tables, scripts, search-on-use, sidebar-filter and tokens-table, the ten in one run of run-node-tests.js as a job runs them (`TEST_SHARD=1/1`, `--test-concurrency=3`: three files at a time, as on a job's 4 cores), on an 11-core Mac, its `# file-duration` lines read by shard-weights.js; and held-room-buttons and held-room-actions, split from held-room-figures when the pages of buttons were added to it, in one such run of the three on 2026-11-27 (held-room-figures took 370 s there, beside them, as it weighs here). Measure those again from CI once a run's jobs are green. Two were weighed from local runs on 2026-11-27, each alone (`--test-concurrency=1`) beside its file's own run before the change, and scaled by that file's weight here: blueprint-pages, 86 s before and 165 s once it read every measure figure in each preset as well (93 × 165 / 86), and held-room-measures, 191 s, beside held-room-tables' 820 s (812 × 191 / 820). forced-layout was weighed from a local run on 2026-11-27 of it beside the five held-room files, blueprint-pages and visuals (`--test-concurrency=2`), where it took 15 s and held-room-tables 805 s for its 812. (The held-room files were one before, and in run 45896337474 it took 321 s in Chromium and 316 s in Firefox before its job was cancelled in WebKit; locally the two took 1187 s in all.) Keep them current: a file they do not weigh, or weigh at half its time, lands in a job it overfills. To measure them again: every job sharded by these weights prints `# file-duration <file> <seconds>` (the duration of the file's own run) at the end of its log; save the logs of a run's jobs (`gh run view -R <owner>/<repo> --job <job> --log > shard-N.log`, or `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/actions/jobs/<job>/logs > shard-N.log`: either can come back empty or end in a stream error, so count each log's `# file-duration` lines) and run `node packages/tools/src/shard-weights.js apps/docs/test/browser/durations.json shard-1.log shard-2.log shard-3.log`. `$alone` lists the files that take a CI job of their own (packages/tools/src/run-node-tests.js, balance): the fixture gallery keeps the job's cores busy for its whole run, and beside it the Button page took more than 30 s to load in WebKit (run 40329390452), so it runs alone and the others share the remaining jobs. The two previews files run alone for the same reason: each draws four pages at a time in Chromium, rastered on the CPU, for its whole run, and beside either one the Button page took 20 to 35 s to load in WebKit and Firefox, often more than `goto`'s 30 s (the Do and Don't, appearance and one-frame tests, in CI and in the CI image). The icon font's test runs alone for the same reason: it opens every built page, four at a time in Chromium, for its whole run, and beside it the Button page took 20 to 32 s to load in WebKit in CI (its share of runs 42696507478, 42708250670 and 42741065358, the last over `goto`'s 30 s); in the CI image on 2 CPUs, its share's files, run as CI runs them, failed 5 to 10 tests in each of 5 runs, the Button page taking 24 to 36 s in WebKit; without it, its other files (once) and the shares the page foot's test has had since (four runs) failed none but the sitemap's test, which dates pages by a commit history the image's copy does not have, the Button page taking 8 to 16 s. The reader's own theme runs alone for the other side of it: it measures how soon a press is drawn (150 ms), and beside other files WebKit drew it in 170 to 210 ms (CI run 42752233102; the CI image on 2 CPUs, three runs of four, two files at a time as well as three), where alone it drew it in 36 to 55 ms (the CI image, five runs measured, and none of eight runs alone failed).
